anchor.statement: Proposition 4.2. The residuals R (0) θ , R (0) z in (4.12) are minus the cylindrical divergences ∂ r + 2/r and ∂r + 1/r of q −A−1/2 T 0 . In particular the equations for vanishing leading residual stress are −2L X ϕ XX + 2 ϕ X ϕ = S q , −2L(XU XX + U X ) = S n . (4.13)

correspondence.note: The residual identities are stated at r > 0, with the stress coefficients identified with the components of F(p_s − s). The equations (4.13) for vanishing stress are not stated as a consequence; only the scalar substitutions behind them appear (StressAlgebra.stressFree_angular_lag_algebra, stressFree_axial_lag_algebra).

links.doc:
Proposition 3.2 for the actual Cartesian Navier--Stokes residual.

The local hypotheses avoid extending the quotient defining radial velocity
across the axis. The two added terms are the exact axial-viscosity terms;
their explicit similarity formulas are `thetaAxialViscosity_eq` and
`axialAxialViscosity_eq`.

                        (NavierStokes.AxisymmetricFields.profilePoint t x) =
